# create-stack

> create-stack starts from a complete app, wires together the pieces you choose, and removes the rest. Pick a framework, database, auth provider, mailer, and optional integrations. The generated project passes typecheck and Biome before it leaves the CLI. Next.js and TanStack Start are supported today.

## How it works

- create-stack starts with a complete base app and keeps only what you select. It adds dependencies, env keys, and composition roots for the selected modules, then removes the rest.
- Requirements: Node >= 22. Works with pnpm, npm, yarn, and bun. MIT licensed and open source.
- The CLI runs typecheck and Biome on the generated project.

## What you can compose

- **Framework**: a complete starter with SSR, routing, Tailwind v4, shadcn, and a theme toggle. Choose Next.js or TanStack Start.
- **Structure**: a standalone app, or an app in `apps/web` inside a Turborepo or Nx monorepo with workspace tasks, caching, and git hooks.
- **Data layer**: Drizzle with Postgres, a driver adapter, schema, seed, and keyset pagination; Prisma; Convex for realtime data; or no database.
- **Auth & API**: better-auth with email and password, verification, and Google OAuth; hosted Clerk; and optional typed tRPC v11 with SSR/RSC support.
- **Mailer**: Resend, Brevo, or SES behind one mailer interface with React Email templates. Change the provider in an env setting.
- **Capabilities**: choose storage (S3/R2/GCS/local), cache (Redis/Upstash/memory), logger (Pino/console), analytics (PostHog/Plausible), background jobs (Inngest), or error tracking (Sentry). The first four support provider swaps. Inngest and Sentry are used directly.
- **Baseline**: strict Biome, typed `env.ts`, a Dockerfile, git hooks, a GitHub Actions CI workflow, and a generated `.env`.
- **UI components**: install components into an existing project with `create-stack add component <name>`. Available components include `date-picker`, `data-table`, and dialogs built on react-call (`confirm`, `alert`, `prompt`, `choice`, `confirm-passphrase`, `confirm-otp`). The dialog `<Root />` is mounted for you.

## Using the UI components

Run inside a generated project. Files are copied into `components/ui`, deps merged, imports
realigned to your alias, and for the dialogs the `<Root />` is mounted in your app shell:

```bash
create-stack add                                      # interactive grouped picker
create-stack add component confirm                    # one component
create-stack add --with component=confirm --with component=prompt
```

The dialogs are built on [react-call](https://react-call.desko.dev) and `await`-ed from
anywhere; their Root is already mounted, so there is nothing to wire:

```tsx
const ok = await Confirm.call({ title: 'Delete project?', variant: 'destructive' })
if (ok) deleteProject()

await Alert.call({ title: 'Saved', description: 'Your changes are live.' })

const name = await Prompt.call({ title: 'Rename', label: 'Name', defaultValue: 'my-app' }) // string | null

const dest = await Choice.call({
  title: 'Move to',
  options: [{ label: 'Inbox', value: 'inbox' }, { label: 'Archive', value: 'archive' }],
}) // string | null

// the confirm button enables only when the input matches the phrase
const confirmed = await ConfirmPassphrase.call({ title: 'Delete repo?', phrase: repo.name })

// verify runs on submit; returning false keeps the dialog open with an error
const verified = await ConfirmOtp.call({ title: 'Enter code', verify: (code) => api.checkOtp(code) })
```

`date-picker` and `data-table` are regular components: `<DatePicker value={date} onChange={setDate} />`
and `<DataTable columns={columns} data={rows} />`.
